channels.title: Ironshell
channels.description:
I spent decades building infrastructure — water systems, power grids, the things people never think about until they stop working. I know how cities stay alive. More importantly, I know exactly how they die. It's never one big explosion. It's a sequence. Pipes first, then pressure, then trust.
This channel isn't about gear lists or tactical fantasies. It's about systems — how they hold, how they fail, and what you can do with what you already have in your house, your neighborhood, your hands. Right now.
I look at historical patterns — New Orleans, Sarajevo, Buenos Aires — because the sequence repeats. Different weather, same breakdown. I look at your water heater, your car battery, your neighbors — because that's where survival actually lives. Not in a $500 backpack.
No panic. No politics. No "smash that like button." Just an old engineer in a dark garage, telling you what breaks first — and what to do before it does. Everything breaks. The question is what breaks first.
